lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: # Deck App Sounds use miniaudio's dev-0.12 branch

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Deck App Sounds play through [miniaudio](https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio)'s engine (`src/audio/sounds.c`), on the host and on the Vita. Released miniaudio (0.11.x) has no Vita backend. The `dev-0.12` branch does: it writes to `sceAudioOut` and runs its mixing thread on `sceKernelCreateThread`, so VitaDeck needs no audio code behind `src/platform/`. `vendor/miniaudio` is a submodule pinned to a commit on that branch, built as its own library with warnings off, like QuickJS.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: raylib's `raudio` is not an option on the Vita: it embeds miniaudio 0.11, and the Vita raylib port builds without it. The host's raylib does embed it, and VitaDeck never calls `InitAudioDevice`, so the two copies never both open a device.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: The engine starts with the first Deck App that declares a sound and stays up until shutdown. Sound files stay encoded in memory and decode on miniaudio's mixing thread, which keeps a long MP3 at its file size. Sounds unload whenever the Deck App stops, at the same point as Deck App Fonts and Images, while the JS thread is stopped; the JS thread then only looks sounds up and calls miniaudio's thread-safe `ma_sound_*` functions.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: **Considered options:** raylib `raudio` (rejected: not built for the Vita, and enabling it there gives miniaudio 0.11 with no Vita backend); miniaudio 0.11 with a custom backend over `sceAudioOut` (rejected: our own threading and port code for what dev-0.12 already ships); SDL2 audio on the Vita (rejected: a second audio stack next to miniaudio on the host).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: **Consequences:** the pin is an unreleased branch. Move it to a 0.12 release when one ships, and test playback on the Vita or in Vita3K whenever the pin moves. Ogg Vorbis needs a decoder miniaudio does not bundle, so sounds are WAV, MP3 and FLAC.
